newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - Gasoline nears seasonal dr.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - Gasoline nears seasonal dr.

text.p: Gasoline may continue to fail in its seasonal role as leader of the barrel this week, traders said, with prices likely to come under fire from bearish fundamentals.
But continued Asian buying of other major products could take up the reins and lend at least some support, traders said.
Gasoline's demise was expected to be limited, with few players keen on running short positions in front of an anticipated seasonal upturn in demand.
"Prices could dip early next week if fundamentals don't improve, but no one will want to sell it too low at this time of year," a trader said.

Ample stocks in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp area and bearish U.S. inventory data pressured prices last week, but traders chalked the supply increases up to refiners "ramping up stocks" ahead of the driving season.
Gas oil is expected to trade sideways this week after the long Easter weekend, with Asian demand potentially drawing more cargoes, traders said.
Russian cargoes were probably going to hold around April IPE flat to +$1.50 cif NWE, but could weaken if the Asian arb starts to lose its lustre.
Diesel was expected to ease after dips last week and the approach of summer grade in two weeks time. Traders say below +$10 cif was likely to be the order of the day.
European naphtha prices showed little sign of recovery from last week's weakness, traders said.
"There's little sign of any real petrochemical buying for lighter grades to come in the short term and only a boost in gasoline demand will help the heavier product," a trader said.

But while the spot market has weakened, forward price indicators have been slower to follow. The April/May contango on swaps widened slightly last week on the anticipated kick-in of the U.S. driving season.
Around 400,000 tonnes is estimated to have sailed East from Europe, pressuring prices in Asia and sealing off arbitrage opportunities.

Fuel oil markets in northern Europe are expected to remain sluggish, with bearish fundamentals defying sellers' attempts to support prices with healthy supply and weak crude prices depressing the market, dealers predict.
Traders saw high sulphur barge prices continuing to sag, with buyers waiting for values to drop below the $80 cif level.
Low sulphur traders in northern Europe will be looking to the Mediterranean for support. But sellers may face competition there from trans-Atlantic supplies, if the arbitrage is open.

Although Italian refinery maintenance will cut the amount of high sulphur available, increased output at one major's Italian plant has satisfied some buyers' April needs, undermining hoped-for price support.

Good flows of Russian and north African straight-run also offer buyers alternatives. Russian E-4, M-40 and M-100 cargoes are appearing in the north with some regularity and were being snapped up by major refiners as cheap alternatives to crude. One trader suggested crude's weakness might end the appetite for Russian cargoes.
